title: 0. Tutorial: First Steps
brief: A guided walk through the controls. Follow the yellow box.
hint: Follow the instructions in the yellow box at the bottom of the screen.

title: 1. Soul Swap
brief: The model sees a red circle. A second run, on a blue circle, is loaded as the transplant source. Copy some of the blue run's cell states into this one.
hint: Go to any low floor (W/S, or click it in the meter), press A to select every picture cell, then Add and bet.
lesson: Transplanting copies cell states from another run; every floor above recomputes from them. If the answer follows, those cells were carrying the information on that floor.

title: 2. Precision Strike
brief: Same swap, but you may only transplant 16 cells. Which part of the picture actually matters?
hint: The circle is in the middle of the board. Drag to paint a block of cells. Does the minimum change from floor to floor?
lesson: Your best cell count is tracked, so go back and try to beat it. In testing, 4 centre cells weren't enough at floors 0-10 but a 4x4 block was.

title: 3. Too Late?
brief: The lower floors are sealed. Transplant picture cells only, from floor 18 up. Somewhere above here it stops working. Find the exact floor.
hint: Bet before each cast. Climb one floor at a time and watch the meter's orange bars.
lesson: On SmolVLM-256M, transplanting the picture works up to floor 22 and fails from 23. By then the colour has been copied out of the picture cells into the text cells, so the picture no longer matters.

title: 4. The Handoff
brief: Now you may NOT touch the picture. Transplant text cells only. Where does the colour arrive?
hint: The answer is read off the very last cell of the text strip. Try just that one cell on different floors.
lesson: Transplanting only the last cell works from floor 23, the mirror image of quest 3. You've located a handoff: floors 22->23 are where 'red' moves from the picture to the answer position. The meter shows the same story.

title: 5. Blackout
brief: No second image this time. Erase the information instead: make the model stop saying red.
hint: 'An average cell' replaces cells with the average picture cell from this same picture. What colour is the average cell of a red-circle picture? Try 'zeros'.
lesson: Erasing every picture cell with the average never removed 'Red' in testing, because the average is still reddish. Zeros are cruder and confuse the model, so it says strange things. In any erasure experiment, what you replace with is part of the answer you get.

title: 6. Left Hand
brief: Asked about the shape on the LEFT, the model says red. Make it say blue by erasing, using at most 32 cells.
hint: Erase the left half of the board (drag across it, or use B for a top-down view).
lesson: With the left shape gone, the model names the colour that remains. It doesn't check 'left' strictly; it falls back on whatever shape it can still see.

title: 7. Paint Without Paint
brief: No second image, no erasing. Push the model's state in the direction from ' red' to ' blue'.
hint: Push from ' red' towards ' blue' (note the leading spaces) on all picture cells around floor 10, strength 4. Then try the last cell only, or a much higher strength.
lesson: Pushing adds a direction instead of copying a whole state. Push too hard and you get 'blue blue blue...'; push only the last cell and the model often breaks. Where you push matters as much as how hard.

title: 8. Read My Lips
brief: The picture contains the word CAT. Make the model read DOG.
hint: Which cells cover the letter C? Which cover the T?
lesson: Text inside images is just more image content. Did you need the whole word, or only some letters? Compare the floors where it works with quests 3 and 4.

title: 9. Open Problem: Counting
brief: Unsolved by the designer. Transplanting the whole picture turns 3 dots into 4. Can you do it with at most 8 cells, and where does the count live? Write down what you find.
hint: No hint. This one's real research.
lesson: If you found a small set of cells, check whether it's 'the fourth dot' or something less obvious. That's how a finding starts.
